briefing.opening: Hello everyone. I will now begin the climate change expert spokesperson briefing for October 7, 2026. Today, we will deliver news on the intensifying global climate crisis warnings, domestic and international efforts towards carbon neutrality and renewable energy transition, and active discussions on climate adaptation and responsibility.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensifying Climate Crisis Warnings and the Urgent Voices of the International Community
sections.content: The news reported today clearly demonstrates the intensifying global climate crisis. A 'Godzilla-level' El Niño phenomenon is causing extreme heat, large-scale floods, landslides, and other abnormal weather events across the globe, breaking temperature records [152, 155]. New Zealand has recorded its highest-ever greenhouse gas concentrations, increasing the risk of heatwaves and droughts, while global water resources are also struggling with drought and heatwaves, raising the possibility of water bill increases [2, 19]. Furthermore, climate health issues, such as heatwaves threatening pregnancy and childbirth, are expected to emerge as a new key agenda item for COP31 [22]. Amidst this crisis, Pacific nations are urgently calling for increased global efforts to achieve the global warming limit targets and for international assistance for their 'survival' [135, 140, 147]. Additionally, two-thirds of global investors have warned that climate physical risks will shake asset prices within five years, expressing concerns about the economic ripple effects [17].

sections.title: 🇰🇷🌱 Acceleration of Domestic 'Green Transformation' and Expansion of Carbon Neutrality Practices
sections.content: Domestically, the 'Green Transformation (K-GX)' strategy, aimed at achieving carbon neutrality and economic growth simultaneously, is gaining momentum. The government has announced plans to invest 1,000 trillion won over the next 10 years to support a major energy transition, including achieving 100GW of renewable energy and expanding the supply of eco-friendly vehicles [25, 26, 27, 36, 69, 77, 105, 109]. In the corporate sector, LG Electronics unveiled its carbon neutrality roadmap for residential spaces, emphasizing the transition to heat pumps, and, together with Samsung Electronics, presented a mid-to-long-term roadmap for achieving carbon neutrality through heating and cooling electrification solutions [24, 35, 46, 60, 67]. Participation from local governments and civil society is also active. The 'Carbon Neutrality Festival' in Suwon City [34], the 'Climate Crisis Carbon Neutrality Education and Upcycling Experience' in Suyeong-gu [29, 51], and the participation of over 4,100 people in carbon neutrality promotion and experiential activities at the Gyeryong Military Culture Festival [31, 49, 53, 57, 61, 62, 65, 66, 68, 73, 74, 76] demonstrate the spreading culture of carbon neutrality practices in daily life. Furthermore, Seongbuk-gu's 'Seongbuk Carbon Neutrality Learning Center' achieved the designation of two environmental education programs as national excellent environmental education programs [38, 55, 56].

sections.title: 🌱⚠️ Acceleration of Renewable Energy Transition and Facing Challenges
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating both domestically and internationally. Through the K-GX strategy, the government aims to achieve a 100GW renewable energy target and will fully embark on a major energy transition through power grid innovation [81, 83, 102, 105, 109]. To achieve these goals, market reforms have also been announced, including the abolition of the Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) spot market and a shift to fixed-price competitive bidding [93]. Overseas, the share of renewable energy in Australia's power grid has surpassed 80%, and investments in renewable energy are expanding, with Meta signing large-scale solar power contracts [84, 90]. Domestic local governments are also active; Cheongyang-gun secured 3.9 billion won in project funds by achieving an 'A grade' in the New and Renewable Energy Convergence and Complex Support Project [80, 87, 97, 101, 116, 117, 121, 127], and Jeonju Hanok Village demonstrated a case of using renewable energy without solar power facilities [98, 113, 120, 131]. However, challenges for a stable transition are also being raised, including delays in solar facility verification [111], concerns about hacking of European renewable energy power plants [122], and the need to strengthen cybersecurity for new and renewable energy [96, 115, 125].

sections.title: 🌍🌱 Legal and Policy Discussions on Climate Adaptation Efforts and Responsibility
sections.content: Legal discussions are actively underway regarding climate change adaptation efforts and the determination of responsibility. Domestically, efforts in the agricultural sector to address climate change are prominent. The Administrator of the Rural Development Administration visited sites for the dissemination of smart agricultural technologies responding to abnormal weather and climate change [11], and the Namwon City Council conducted benchmarking of agricultural sites responding to climate change [12, 15], indicating high interest in crop breeding and alternative crop development [13, 146]. Internationally, in Australia, the High Court ruled in favor of a Hunter Valley community group in a landmark climate change-considered lawsuit concerning the approval of the Mount Pleasant coal mine, setting a national precedent for fossil fuel projects [144, 154, 156]. The U.S. Supreme Court has also begun to address whether fossil fuel companies are immune from climate change damage lawsuits, expanding discussions on legal responsibility [142, 143, 145]. Additionally, international cooperation and education for climate crisis response continue steadily, with site managers of Ghana's World Heritage castles receiving climate crisis response training in Korea [18] [16, 21, 23].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has once again confirmed the severity of the global climate crisis, while simultaneously demonstrating the active and multifaceted efforts and discussions underway, both domestically and internationally, to overcome it. Responding to climate change is no longer an option but a necessity, and a sustainable future can only be built when scientific knowledge, civic participation, and policy support are harmonized. This concludes today's climate briefing.

summary.phenomenon: According to a study by the London School of Economics, scientists who believe technology will largely solve the problems caused by the climate crisis are less likely to engage in civic action on climate issues. They are 23% less likely to sign petitions or participate in protests than peers who doubt that technology is the answer, and 18% less likely to make high-impact lifestyle changes.
summary.cause: This behavior is attributed to 'techno-optimism,' which may lead to reliance on unproven solutions at the expense of necessary societal changes.
